content:
Aria: Heads up — customers reporting sporadic out-of-order SSE frames after autoscaling events. Noticed it mostly on multiplexed sessions and higher fanout.
Ben: any recent autoscaler changes or routing tweaks?
Aria: autoscaler ramp change yesterday to be more aggressive about draining hot sockets during scale-up. suspect race between drain + resume acceptance.
Cassie: logs from edge show this pattern:
```
[2026-04-02T21:03:10Z] node=eu-a drain=start session=s-204
[2026-04-02T21:03:10Z] node=eu-a emit frame=201 session=s-204
[2026-04-02T21:03:10Z] router: resume routed to eu-b for token=tok-zzz
[2026-04-02T21:03:10Z] node=eu-b emit frame=202 session=s-204
[2026-04-02T21:03:10Z] client_recv frame=202
[2026-04-02T21:03:11Z] client_recv frame=201
```
Aria: so old node emitted 201 but client sees 202 first. Not huge window but breaks some clients that assume monotonic frames.
Riley: probably because we allowed the old node to finish emitting during drain but didn't coordinate resume acceptance exclusivity. Two simultaneous emitters for same session.
Ben: trade-offs here: strict single-emitter (handshake flush) eliminates reorder but introduces handoff latency and may increase dropped messages under heavy load. Relaxed model reduces drops but risks reorders/double-delivery.
Marta (console): product impact: console "active_streams" and "inflight_frames" look noisy; support tickets complaining about message order. Want to show a brief badge on route pages for "handoff turbulence" while infra triages.
Cassie: quick telemetry we can add: runtime.stream.handoff_reorder when adjacent frame ids are received out-of-order within 2s, plus sampled trace capture of the involved emitters.
Aria: also propose a short-term config: limit drain mode to emit-only after suspend_accept for 50ms for multiplexed sessions, effectively preventing new resume acceptance for that brief window so only old node can finish.
Riley: can do, but that means a reconnect during that 50ms will route to another node which will be refused (resume rejected) and client must retry -> potential UX blip.
Ben: alternative short-term: keep relaxed acceptance but add server-side dedupe at delivery: maintain a tiny recent-frame-set per-session (last N frame checksums) and drop duplicates on arrival at client-facing plane. This avoids duplicate billing but not reorder.
Cassie: implementing checksum dedupe is cheap memory-wise if we limit to N=8 frames per session and TTL=5s. It helps billing/dedupe but doesn't fix ordering.
Marta (console): console wants signal, not invisibility. If we do dedupe we still need to show a badge and a tooltip: "Some sessions may see duplicate or out-of-order frames during node handoffs."
Ben: metrics to expose for gating rollout: handoff_reorder_rate, dedupe_drop_count, resume_reject_rate. We can gate full strict-handshake only if handoff_reorder_rate > 0.1% and dedupe_drop_count > threshold.
Aria: I can prototype the drain-suspend tweak behind a feature flag scoped to mp sessions. Minimal patch:```
--- a/routing/drain.go
+++ b/routing/drain.go
@@ -88,6 +88,12 @@ func beginDrain(node) {
  node.setDrain(true)
+  if node.session.IsMultiplexed() {
+    node.suspendResumeAccept(50 * time.Millisecond)
+  }
 }
```
Riley: I'll sketch the checksum ring buffer in proxy and emit runtime.stream.dedupe_{inc,drop}.
DeployBot: starting canary: runtime/routing/2026-04-02/drain-suspend-plus-dedupe -> eu-canary (id: d-10123).
DeployBot: canary finished: 5/5 healthy.
Aria: early canary metrics: handoff_reorder_rate down from 0.42% -> 0.06% on mp routes; dedupe_drop_count=12 in 30m on canary hosts. Looks promising.
Marta (console): I'll add the "handoff turbulence" badge to route pages and a small link to the incident note. Low-risk UI change.
Ben: next steps: 1) collect 6h of canary metrics, 2) if stable widen rollout; 3) long-term decision: tradeoff doc on strict handshake vs resume-suspend pattern + small dedupe buffer.
Cassie: I'll upload the sampled traces for the dedupe drops to the tracing bucket for root-cause analysis.
Aria: thanks team. We'll reconvene after 6h and decide whether to widen the rollout or try a smaller handshake variant.
